chapter: Harry James, Bellson and the return to Duke
title: Segregation incidents with Willie Smith in the James band
summary: Willard asks about trouble over Willie Smith's race in the South; Tizol recalls little, and Rose says James once refused segregated audiences.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Do you remember any incidents when Willie was in Harry's band? I remember the one that Willie told me about traveling in the south, but -- the fact that some southerners would know that Willie was really colored -- was there ever any incident where anybody tried to make any trouble because he was playing with a white band?
Oh, that was down south somewhere, when we got back together before.
I'm talking about when we already recorded.

When we talked about Duke's band -- I'm talking about Willie in Harry James' band. Because I remember that Willie told me about how one time they came looking for him because they heard they were coming to town and they had laws against mixed bands.
Oh, that was down South, yes.
Yeah, down South. Did that happen often? I remember one time Willie told me.
No, I don't know about any more.
And didn't Harry James refuse to play for segregated audiences down south? Do you remember?
No, I don't know anything about that.
I think he did one time, Juan.
